ECDSAInvalidSignatureS(bytes32).details: The signature has an S value that is in the upper half order.

OwnableInvalidOwner(address).details: The owner is not a valid owner account. (eg. `address(0)`)

OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(address).details: The caller account is not authorized to perform an operation.

acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

params.scores: decrypted scores in join order (0 = unfunded entry, else multiplier + 1)

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

InvalidKMSSignatures().notice: Returned if the returned KMS signatures are not valid.

SenderNotAllowedToUseHandle(bytes32,addr.notice: Returned if the sender is not allowed to use the handle.

ZamaProtocolUnsupported().notice: Returned if the Zama protocol is not supported on the current chain

PublicDecryptionVerified(bytes32[],bytes.notice: This event is emitted when public decryption has been successfully verified.

MAX_ENTRY_AGE().notice: The entry price of a solo run must be at most this old (Sepolia inclusion can take         a few blocks); a fallback price can ride along to refresh it in the same transaction.

RESERVE_REFILL().notice: House bankroll top-up (testnet: USDCMock is publicly mintable), in token units.

SCALE().notice: Multipliers are fixed point with 6 decimals: 1_000_000 = the stake back.

authorizeSession(address,uint64,bytes).notice: Lets a browser session key act for the caller (start runs, join rounds, cash out),         so a run needs no wallet pop-up. The session proves it consents by signing         `sessionDigest(player, expiry)`. Any ETH sent is forwarded to the session for gas.         A session can only play with the stake the player approved (ERC-7984 operator);         it can never withdraw.

cashOut(uint256,bytes[]).notice: Ends the caller's run now (solo: paid in the same transaction; round: the exit is         recorded and scored on ciphertexts). A signed Pyth update can ride along so the         exit is the freshest verified price.

claim(uint256).notice: Permissionless: pays a round run what it is owed, its prize once the round is         finalized, or its entry back (the encrypted amount it paid) if the round was refunded.         One transfer per transaction keeps every payout under the per-transaction gas cap,         even when many players tie for a prize.

closeRound(uint256).notice: Permissionless, after the round's end: every run still climbing exits at the bell,         and every encrypted score becomes publicly decryptable (the standings reveal).

exitAtBell(uint256).notice: Permissionless, after the round's end: one run still climbing exits at the bell.         Each exit costs about 1M gas on Sepolia, so a full round is closed in chunks: exits         first (any number of transactions), then `closeRound` (cheap once every run exited).

finalizeRound(uint256,uint32[],bytes).notice: Permissionless: verifies the decrypted standings with the KMS proof, ranks the         players and pays the pot (50 / 30 / 20 %, ties share their places).

joinRound(uint256,bytes32,bytes).notice: Joins round `roundId` with an encrypted side; the entry is a public amount moved         as an encrypted transfer. Joining `roundCount()` while no round is open opens it         on `nextRoundMarket()`.

ladder().notice: The ladder rules: what a long and a short make on the oracle path of a run.

nextRoundMarket().notice: Market of the next round to open: the next one in the rotation that has a live         price (a checkpoint in the last 60 s), so a round never opens on a closed market.

openPack().notice: Draws a leverage pack with the FHEVM encrypted PRNG. The tier stays encrypted         (only the player can decrypt it): Bronze 45 %, Silver 28 %, Gold 18 %, Diamond 9 %.         A packed run caps its ladder at the pack's leverage, selected on ciphertexts.

playerOf(address).notice: The player a caller acts for: the session's player, or the caller itself.

prizeOf(uint256).notice: Prize owed to a round run (plaintext: standings are public at finalize), paid by `claim`.

publishRun(uint256).notice: Owner of a finished solo run: reveal its result for the leaderboard. Makes the         run's multiplier publicly decryptable (the stake stays private).

recordRun(uint256,uint32,bytes).notice: Permissionless: records a published run with the KMS decryption proof.

refundRound(uint256).notice: Permissionless safety valve: a round the KMS never finalized refunds every entry.

reserveFloor().notice: Lower bound of the house's cUSDC that is not yet promised to a live solo run.

roundMarkets(uint256).notice: Markets rounds rotate over (Pyth-verified ones: players compete with each other).

roundScoreHandles(uint256).notice: Score handles of a round, in join order (publicly decryptable once closed).

sessionDigest(address,uint64).notice: What a session key signs (EIP-191) to accept acting for `player`.

settleRun(uint256).notice: Permissionless: settles a solo run whose 60 seconds are over, at its last second.

startRun(uint8,bytes32,bytes32,bytes,boo.notice: Opens a solo run. Side and stake are encrypted inputs (bound to the caller); the         stake is clamped to `MAX_STAKE` on ciphertexts and pulled from the player as an         ERC-7984 operator. A signed Pyth update can ride along so the entry is fresh; for a         market Pyth does not cover, a public price can ride along instead (the oracle's         bounds apply, exactly as for `pushPublic`).

userdoc.notice: The Sirocco climbing game on the Zama Protocol: pick a market, go long or short, the         leverage climbs from 1x to 4x every 6 seconds over a 60 second run, cash out whenever. What is confidential (see README, "Confidentiality design"):  - the side (long / short) of every run is an encrypted `ebool`: nobody can copy or fade a    player, or the crowd of a round;  - the stake of a solo run is an encrypted `euint64` in Zama's confidential USDC (ERC-7984);  - a run's value is computed on ciphertexts: the contract computes, in clear, what a long and    a short would have made on the public oracle path (`multLong`, `multShort`), then picks one    with the encrypted side (`FHE.select`) and multiplies the encrypted stake by it. The payout    is an encrypted transfer in the same transaction: money never waits for a decryption;  - round standings stay encrypted while the round is live and are revealed once at the end by    public decryption, verified on chain with the KMS proof (`FHE.checkSignatures`);  - leverage packs are drawn with the on-chain encrypted PRNG and stay private: a packed run's    leverage cap is selected on ciphertexts. Every lifecycle step after a player's own action is permissionless (`settleRun`, `closeRound`, `finalizeRound`, price pushes), so the players' browsers can run the game with nothing else.
